speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Has she experienced any recent fevers, headaches, or neck stiffness that might suggest an infection like meningitis? I also need to know if she has a history of autoimmune diseases or if she has been taking any new medications recently.

speaker: Doctor

text: Past medical history: Patient has a history of hypertension, managed with medication. No other significant medical history is reported. Social history: Patient is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Drinks alcohol socially. No illicit drug use is reported.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, seizure, vision changes, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, recent illness, or fever. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Your sodium level is critically low at 122 mEq/L, which explains your confusion and lethargy. To determine the cause of this hyponatremia, REQUEST TEST: Serum_Osmolality and REQUEST TEST: Urine_Sodium.

speaker: Doctor
text: The low serum osmolality confirms true hyponatremia, and the high urine sodium indicates euvolemic or hypervolemic status rather than dehydration. Given your smoking history and these findings, I suspect SIADH, possibly due to an underlying lung malignancy. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CTA

text: The patient's history of gastroenteritis likely led to excessive hypotonic fluid intake or medication effects causing SIADH, rather than a malignancy given the lack of respiratory symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH)
